searchText: <@397389662085185547> I violated rules? What's wrong? technical debate Correct **technical** debate This is a debate on the merge timing Which is **technical** You always seem to be very angry or upset all the time for some reason, I have no idea why. Saying developers will be held liable for losses if the merge goes wrong is a subtle but innocuous threat of sorts. Saying a beacon chain sync takes months is also wrong (have you actually ever tried to sync to head?). Also why you disagree with me? Who takes responsibility if user funds are lost (either via panic selloff either via protocol loss) in your opinion then? _You_ do I didn't say that Beacon chain sync takes month. I said that it will take months for users to take action. If you don't want to run the fork, then don't. But either way, this server is not about legal talk I don't agree on merge and I don't want it Why would I be responsible? Then fork off? The value of ETH is persistent only on the main chain I mean that I'm not responsible for something I didn't do Let's make a thread because it goes off topic Oof, that won't hold up well in court in general. But again, this server is for technical discussions. > You always seem to be very angry or upset all the time for some reason, I have no idea why. I thought this was obvious <@813143648471482378> these posts aren’t useful. This server is meant for technical discussion and there really isn’t anything productive that can come out of an exchange framed this way. We will ban you if you keep it up. While I do agree that this is off-topic, I still think that there should be a place where people can raise their concerns about Ethereum. At the end, they are honest holders that represent a stake in the Ethereum ecosystem. <@354681205842771973> sure, there are plenty: reddit, twitter, ethereum-magicians, etc. That said, these high-level conversations, often about topics where the vast majority of the community is already on board with, aren't the best fit for this server, which is focused on discussing the technicals of various areas of R&D related to Ethereum. To use The Merge as an example, it's been over 1 year that client teams have started prototyping it and we are months away from shipping it on mainnet. The time for making a case "against PoS" at a technical level was well before now. If you still disagree, that's fine, and there are plenty of places to rally parts of the community on that front, just not the server where everyone who is actually working on it is. But even disregarding the specific topic, stuff like: > Damn so when pos fails and crashes all the devs are going pull a Luna and blame the users that staked into the platform? That’s cold af and show this point once again just isn't appropriate for this server. It's not actionable, and at best passive-aggressive towards everyone trying to engage in civil discourse here. ^ I've said before to Alex and Chs2 that if they had a serious reason for why the merge shouldn't happen then the time to raise it was >1 year ago and it's far too late now Hey don’t bring me in 😂 For ethereum-magicians: It is not being read by regular people, only hardcore enthusiasts and core devs. For reddit: r/ethereum is full with Merge shills who don't understand anything technical but just "PoS will make $ETH go to the moon". They'll downvote your post to the bottom which will make your the community reach non-existent. For twitter: You can reach your followers only. Eth R&D is the only place where Ethereum users can directly talk to the core devs My recent comments are mostly regarding testnets along with some sarcasm and helpful stuff😅 eth mining is barely break even these days My apologies if I'm misremembering which conversations are which, having the same profile picture is confusing
